## What it is

This project aims to use machine learning to predict whether severe workplace injuries catalogued by OSHA involved hospitalization of an injured worker. 
In doing so it compares the outcomes of 3 different model types (random forest, support vector classification, and K-nearest neighbors) and two data input types (structured categorical vs. unstructured text data) to investigate what the most accurate combination is. 
Somewhat surprisingly, the best-performing model was a text-based support vector classification model, suggesting that text narratives of incidents can be a robust source of information relating to incident outcomes. 

## What I did

- Led the cleaning and pre-processing of OSHA severe injury data.
- Created 6 classification models (3 based on categorical variables, 3 based on text descriptions of events) to predict whether or not a given injury ended in hospitalization.
- Presented findings as both a slideshow and Jupyter notebook.
